title: Checks for operations where precedence may be unclear and suggests to add parentheses.
summary: It catches a mixed usage of arithmetic and bit shifting/combining operators, as well as method calls applied to closures. Not everyone knows the precedence of those operators by heart, so expressions like these may trip others trying to reason about the code. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for bit shifting operations combined with bit masking/combining operators and suggest using parentheses.
summary: Not everyone knows the precedence of those operators by heart, so expressions like these may trip others trying to reason about the code. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of println, print, eprintln or eprint in an implementation of a formatting trait.
summary: Using a print macro is likely unintentional since formatting traits should write to the Formatter, not stdout/stderr. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: This lint warns about the use of literals as print!/println! args.
summary: Using literals as println! args is inefficient (c.f., https://github.com/matthiaskrgr/rust-str-bench) and unnecessary (i.e., just put the literal in the format string) Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for printing on stderr.
summary: The purpose of this lint is to catch debugging remnants. People often print on stderr while debugging an application and might forget to remove those prints afterward. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for printing on stdout.
summary: The purpose of this lint is to catch debugging remnants. People often print on stdout while debugging an application and might forget to remove those prints afterward. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: This lint warns when you use print!() with a format string that ends in a newline.
summary: You should use println!() instead, which appends the newline. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: This lint warns when you use println!("") to print a newline.
summary: You should use println!(), which is simpler. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.
